item.title: Emmanuel Acho believes Steve Sarkisian’s Texas offense is unbeatable, but there’s a catch
item.description: Scott Wachter-Imagn Images Emmanuel Acho believes Steve Sarkisian’s Texas offense is unbeatable, but there’s a catch appeared first on ClutchPoints . Emmanuel Acho has a lot of confidence in Steve Sarkisian and the Texas Longhorns being the best team in the country as they get through the ups and downs of the 2026 campaign. Texas got off to a promising start, winning its first four games and rising to No. 1 of the AP Top 25. They have since lost two consecutive games against Oklahoma and Florida in collapsing fashion, free falling down to 19th in the latest rankings. Acho watched Texas’ latest contest against Ole Miss on Saturday. Seeing how the Longhorns returned to solid form against one of the best teams in the country, the sports personality had a bold take regarding the Longhorns’ talent against the best. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “If every college football team in the Nation is at their best, @TexasFootball is the best team in the nation,” Acho wrote. If every college football team in the Nation is at their best, @TexasFootball is the best team in the nation. pic.twitter.com/hYAHAtCWJn — Emmanuel Acho (@EmmanuelAcho) October 25, 2026 How Steve Sarkisian, Texas performed against Ole Miss Steve Sarkisian and Texas made their way back to the win column. They picked up a valuable 34-27 win over the No. 7 Ole Miss Rebels. Their standing in the AP Top 25 will improve after stunning one of the best SEC squads in the country. Texas did most of its damage in the first half, boasting a 24-3 lead at halftime. Ole Miss attempted a rally with 24 points in the second half, but the Longhorns made enough plays down the stretch to stop the collapse from happening for the third consecutive game. Arch Manning racked up multiple touchdowns to his name as he gets back on track. He completed 18 out of 30 passes for 212 yards and a touchdown and two interceptions while rushing eight times for two yards and two touchdowns. Raleek Brown commanded the run game with 23 carries for 157 yards. As for the receivers, Ryan Wingo topped the group with seven catches for 111 yards and a touchdown. The No. 19 Longhorns will look forward to their next matchup, remaining at home. They host the Mississippi State Bulldogs in Week 9 as kickoff commences on Oct. 31 at 7:30 p.m. ET. item.title: Arch Manning showed shades of uncle Peyton Manning with his winning touchdown against Ole Miss
item.description: Credit: Johnnie Izquierdo/Ezra Shaw via Getty Images Arch Manning is hoping to be the first third-generation NFL quarterback from the legendary Manning family, and he’s already tapping into the family moves. Manning is currently with the Texas Longhorns and helped them achieve a big win against #7-ranked Ole Miss on Saturday night. Perhaps no play of his had more impact on the game than his fourth-quarter TD to give the Longhorns the lead they held on to earn a win. Arch Manning scores identical touchdown to Peyton Manning from his Broncos days During the fourth quarter, Arch Manning and the Longhorns were just a few yards away from the end zone. Rather than an intricate play, Manning faked the handoff to calmly bring the ball into the end zone himself. One fan noticed how similar this play was to one that his uncle, Peyton Manning, once ran with the Denver Broncos against the Dallas Cowboys. Understandably, many fans were quick to point out how similar the plays were, with many suggesting that the play was a Manning Dynasty special. One conflicted fan simply wrote: “As a die-hard Cowboys and Longhorns fan, I can’t explain how this touchdown made me feel.” Another fan joked: “That’s the Uncle Peyton special.” A third fan joked that the commentator saw the Texans QB channelling his uncle: “Herbstreit absolutely called that live on air.” A fourth fan suggested that the origin of Peyton’s play was during his college days: “Show the real highlight – Uncle Peyton doing at Tennessee vs. Alabama.” A fifth fan added: “A Manning on a bootleg is pure football comedy gold. Best QB bit?” And lastly, one final fan in attendance shared a similar family story: “No joke I turned to my grandpa in the stadium when this happened and told him about Peyton doing it.” Manning has shown similar flashes of brilliance from the quarterback position that fans have become accustomed to seeing from the Manning dynasty members. While he didn’t have a perfect game against Ole Miss, Manning delivered a performance that he desperately needed. item.title: Brewers make postseason history with incredible merchandise sales record
item.description: Michael McLoone-Imagn Images. Brewers make postseason history with incredible merchandise sales record appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Milwaukee Brewers are two wins away from taking down the Tampa Bay Rays for their first World Series title , and their fans have already made history of their own. The Brewers have sold more merchandise this postseason than any team in MLB history, according to Bob Nightengale of USA Today . MLB officials shared the news with Brewers owner Mark Attanasio amid the team’s historic October run. It is the latest sign of just how much this October has meant to Milwaukee. The Brewers are back in the Fall Classic for the first time since 1982 , when they fell to the St. Louis Cardinals in seven games, and the city has fully embraced the moment. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The record did not come out of nowhere. Fans started lining up for gear long before the World Series arrived. After the Brewers swept the Los Angeles Dodgers to win the National League pennant, an MLB spokesperson told the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel that sales exploded over the next two days. “More Brewers merch was sold in those 48 hours than any other pennant winner on record,” the spokesperson said. According to the Journal Sentinel, Milwaukee topped the previous mark held by the 2022 Philadelphia Phillies by about 5%. The Brewers also beat the 2025 Chicago Cubs’ NLCS sales by 14% and the 2024 Dodgers by 60%. Brewers fans set an all-time record for sales of NLCS locker room-style shirts as well. The players have given those fans plenty to celebrate. Milwaukee has won seven straight games, including a 3-2 victory over the Rays in Game 1 of the World Series. On Saturday, the Brewers erased an early four-run deficit and held on for a 5-4 win in Game 2, taking a 2-0 series lead. Sal Frelick tied the game with a solo homer in the sixth , and Cooper Pratt delivered the go-ahead single in the seventh . Aaron Ashby then stranded the tying run at third in the ninth to seal it and extend his scoreless postseason run . If the Brewers finish the job, the merchandise record could grow even more. Championship gear is always in high demand, and a city that has waited this long for a title would likely be first in line. Game 3 is set for Monday at Tropicana Field. item.title: Alexander Volkanovski Refused to Take Even Ibuprofen Despite Being Extremely Sick at UFC 333
item.description: UFC 333 turned into another memorable night for Alexander Volkanovski. The 38-year-old overcame another challenge to defend his featherweight title at Etihad Arena, finishing Movsar Evloev in the second round and handing the Russian his first career loss after 20 straight wins. As expected, Volkanovski’s sharp striking and excellent takedown defense made the difference. He looked quicker from the opening bell, targeting Evloev’s legs with inside low kicks before mixing in stiff jabs and powerful overhand rights. Volkanovski eventually hurt Evloev with a big overhand right before following up with a flurry of punches that sent the Russian crashing to the canvas. He kept attacking until referee Marc Goddard stepped in with just seconds left in the second round . But the win became even more impressive after it emerged that Volkanovski had been battling the flu during fight week. The champion reportedly refused to take any medication, believing it could give him an unfair advantage over his opponent. Alexander Volkanovski Refused Medication at UFC 333 Because He Feared It Would Be Unfair to Movsar Evloev The signs were there during Friday’s early-morning weigh-ins, when Volkanovski’s voice sounded noticeably different. Many initially put it down to the weight cut, but his training partner and BJJ legend Craig Jones later revealed on social media that the Aussie had been sick. Jones shared a picture of Volkanovski with the featherweight title and captioned it, “flu game @alexandervolkanovski.” View this post on Instagram A post shared by Craig Jones (@craigjonesbjj) Volkanovski also confirmed at the UFC 333 post-fight press conference that he wasn’t feeling 100% going into the fight. However, the champion seemed to take the setback in stride, even joking that it would have been too easy if he hadn’t gotten sick. He said with a smile, “Ah, good enough to get out there and get it done. I mean, yeah, it’s all good. It’s a part of the game. A part of the challenges that I like anyway. item.title: Steven Gerrard praises Bayern Munich star Harry Kane
item.description: Photo by Will Palmer/Sportsphoto/Allstar via Getty Images | Getty Images With the Ballon d’Or ceremony starting in a few days, Harry Kane is leading the race to win the award. The Bayern Munich striker has the endorsement of numerous English players, including legends of the game like Steven Gerrard, showing their admiration for the England captain and indirectly helping his case to win it. The former Liverpool midfielder praised the 33-year-old ahead of Bayern’s 2-2 draw with Arsenal. “Let’s all just enjoy greatness because that’s what he is,” Gerrard said (TNT as captured by X account @iMiaSanMia ). “You know, he’s arguably the best English player that’s ever been and that’s the biggest compliment I can pay him. Because if you think about the greats that we’ve had, Harry Kane’s in that conversation.” Declan Rice, Morgan Rogers and Jude Bellingham all indicated being in favor of a Kane Ballon d’Or win; Rice and Bellingham are Ballon d’Or nominees themselves. Although Gerrard did not explicitly back Kane to win the award, he joins Alan Shearer, Gary Lineker, Rio Ferdinand, Michael Owen, Peter Crouch, and many English greats on the growing list of admirers of the 33-year-old. item.title: The Army Officer playing for Wales at a World Cup
item.description: Jade Mullen is the captain of the Army rugby union team [WALES RUGBY LEAGUE] Jade Mullen's journey to the Women's Rugby League World Cup has been an unconventional one. A last-minute code switch within the sport allowed her to earn a place in Wales' squad for the showpiece tournament in Australia. Mullen has plenty of rugby union experience having captained the Army's team at high-profile venues like Twickenham. But she had never played rugby league before January this year. That changed when Wales captain Bethan Dainton, who is also enlisted in the British Army, encouraged her to try the 13-a-side game. She started training with London Broncos and the rest, as they say, is history. "Me and Bethan have been close friends for a few years. She's played rugby league much longer than me and she always said that I'd enjoy it, so I thought I'd give it a go," said Mullen. "I joined London Broncos at the start of the season so was training with them from January onwards ready for the season to kick off in March. I fell in love with the sport so I'm really enjoying it. "For a while I was training twice a week at London Broncos and then also doing rugby union training at the same time. That was tiring." Mullen's venture into rugby league has paid off. Not only has she represented Wales in both games so far at the World Cup in Australia, she also was part of the London Broncos squad that won the National Championship to earn promotion to the Super League. During that period she also had to play for the Army, and is grateful to the Broncos for their support. "Luckily London Broncos were really understanding. They knew that the Army is my full-time job and that I was captain of the team, so they were really supportive of me," Mullen said. item.title: 'He’s ready!' – Luis Enrique speaks out on Ukrainian defender Illia Zabarnyi
item.description: FBL-FRA-LIGUE1-PSG-LE MANS - AFP PSG head coach Luis Enrique hailed the rapid development of Ukrainian centre-back Illia Zabarnyi since joining the club. The manager expressed delight with the defender's growing composure following a trophy-laden debut season in Paris. Zabarnyi continues impressive rise in Paris Saint-Germain defense Ukrainian centre-back Illia Zabarnyi has established himself as a vital figure in Paris Saint-Germain's backline under head coach Luis Enrique. The 24-year-old made history as PSG's first-ever Ukrainian player after joining on a permanent five-year contract in August 2025. Zabarnyi enjoyed a sensational debut season in the French capital, winning four major trophies including the UEFA Champions League. The defender scored his first goal for the club during a 2-0 league victory over Auxerre last season. Luis Enrique highlights defender's experience and composure Luis Enrique lauded Zabarnyi's ability to adapt seamlessly to an elite environment after making his debut in a 1-0 win against Nantes. item.title: Hoeneß claims Wirtz "would play much better" for Bayern than Liverpool
item.description: Hoeneß claims Wirtz "would play much better" for Bayern than Liverpool Uli Hoeneß has revealed in an interview that he is still annoyed that Florian Wirtz's transfer to Bayern Munich didn't go through in 2025. “No. Because Florian would play much better for us than he does at Liverpool," Bayern's honorary president told Welt am Sonntag. “I watch many of the team’s [Liverpool's] games. They simply haven’t integrated him properly at all. “In Leverkusen he got every ball, in Liverpool he’s just one among many,” said Hoeneß, noting how the midfielder in no longer a focal point. However, Hoeneß was quick to rule out the German record champions as a fallback option for Wirtz to reignite his career. "No. He has a long-term contract in Liverpool. They will try to integrate him better there," he said of the Reds' €125million signing. Wirtz's form has recently even shown some improvement. Nevertheless, transfer rumors away from Merseyside still persist.

item.title: Will IPL 2027 be MS Dhoni's last dance? CSK legend drops big hint
item.description: NEW DELHI: Will MS Dhoni return for another season of the Indian Premier League (IPL), or is the former India captain close to calling time on his career? The questions around his future continue as fans wait to know whether he will play in IPL 2027. Dhoni has now offered a hint about his plans. The 45-year-old said he would first check his fitness before deciding whether he could play another season. He missed the entire IPL 2026 season due to fitness issues, mainly related to his calf. Dhoni to assess fitness before December Asked about his plans to play another IPL season, Dhoni responded with humour while making it clear that his fitness would be the deciding factor. "Doc, I will have to go through the test. You will have to give me the report, and then before December, I will have to see, you know, how strong I am to maybe play one more season," Dhoni said. He then joked about the responsibility of keeping him fit for another season. "And if I am not, then, you know, you will have to make sure that you do everything right with me and make sure that this old vintage vehicle is running well on the road. So all the pressure is on them," he added. Dhoni's comments indicate that he could decide on his IPL future before December. However, he has not confirmed whether he will return to the field for IPL 2027. Dhoni's role in CSK has changed Dhoni's role in Chennai Super Kings' batting line-up has gradually reduced over the past few years. He has mostly batted in the final overs, looking to score quick runs and give fans a glimpse of his trademark power-hitting. Even with a smaller role, Dhoni remains one of the leading run-scorers in IPL history. He has scored 5,439 runs in 278 matches at an average of 38.30. His record includes 24 half-centuries in 242 innings. His success as a captain has been equally impressive. Dhoni led CSK to five IPL titles and also guided the franchise to two Champions League T20 titles. CSK struggle to match Dhoni's success CSK have struggled to achieve the same success since Ruturaj Gaikwad took over as captain in 2024. The team finished at the bottom of the table in IPL 2025 before managing an eighth-place finish in IPL 2026. CSK last won the IPL title in 2023, when Dhoni was leading the side.

item.title: David Raum: Man United target makes feelings clear on potential January move
item.description: David Raum: Man United target makes feelings clear on potential January move Manchester United’s pursuit of RB Leipzig captain David Raum appears to have taken an optimistic turn. The Red Devils were looking to add more cover for Luke Shaw this summer and had the German speedster on their wish list. Unfortunately, the English giants failed to strengthen the position before the end of the transfer window. United have lived to regret that decision, as Shaw has appeared in only five of the 11 games in all competitions. The Red Devils have also struggled to impress in the final third, managing just two wins this season. The situation has prompted calls for squad reinforcements at the turn of the year. It now appears that United could return for Raum in January. United prioritising January move for Raum According to Daily Debrief , United have made David Raum their priority target for the winter transfer window. The report states: “Manchester United are ready to shift their transfer focus towards strengthening the defence in January, with RB Leipzig captain David Raum emerging as one of the leading targets.” “After significant investment elsewhere in Michael Carrick’s squad, left-back and centre-back are now considered priority areas.” “Raum appears to be the most attainable high-level option, while Alejandro Balde, Adrien Truffert and Jarrad Branthwaite are also being monitored.” Raum’s contract expires at the end of this season, and he is yet to sign a new deal. D. Raum Raum interested in Premier League move The report goes on to state that Raum is keen to test himself in the Premier League. With the player’s contract expiring in less than 12 months, January could be an ideal opportunity for Leipzig to cash in on him. The report adds that United are in a good position in the race for the 28-year-old, who could hit the ground running at Old Trafford. It is believed that the German is open to the prospect of joining the English giants. The Red Devils could also target a new centre-back in January, so the opportunity to sign Raum for a nominal fee would appeal to them. That could leave funds available for INEOS to invest in someone like Jarrad Branthwaite, although he is likely to cost a small fortune. Balde could be another option for the English giants to explore in January, especially since he has struggled for game time with Barcelona this season. Final Thoughts Raum’s attacking instincts, experience, and leadership qualities make him an ideal candidate for United in January. The Red Devils, as such, must make every effort to secure the RB Leipzig captain’s signature at the turn of the year. item.title: Bayern bosses offer differing assessments of Lennart Karl’s development
item.description: Bayern bosses offer differing assessments of Lennart Karl’s development Bayern Munich honorary president and supervisory board member Uli Hoeneß has spoken strongly about Lennart Karl, insisting that the highly rated youngster is still far from being a superstar. In an interview with WELT , the Bayern legend revealed that he intends to speak directly with the 18-year-old. “I’m planning to have a serious talk with him. He’s far from being a superstar; young players need humility. Comparisons to Olise are clearly not doing him any good; there’s still a world of difference between them,” the 74-year-old stated. Karl enjoyed an impressive breakthrough season with Bayern last term. The winger scored five goals and provided five assists in the Bundesliga, while adding four goals and two assists in the Champions League. His momentum was interrupted shortly before the World Cup when he suffered a thigh muscle injury that ruled him out of the tournament. Since returning, Karl has yet to rediscover the form he showed during his breakthrough campaign. Max Eberl backs Karl amid Hoeneß criticism Asked about Hoeneß’s comments, Bayern Board Member for Sport Max Eberl offered a more measured assessment of Karl’s development and stressed the impact of his injury layoff. “What’s happening with Lenny is a completely normal process for a young player. We’re supporting him and are convinced he’ll reach that level again. But he had the injury, he missed the World Cup, and that naturally has an impact on a player,” Eberl said. Hoeneß’s comments underline the high expectations surrounding Karl following his breakthrough campaign, while Eberl’s response reflects Bayern’s desire to give the youngster time to rediscover his best form after a disruptive few months. GGFN | Brook Genene

item.title: Movsar Evloev Issues Statement After UFC 333 TKO Loss
item.description: Movsar Evloev UFC 333 Getty UFC featherweight contender Movsar Evloev issued a statement after his UFC 333 knockout loss against Alexander Volkanovski. Evloev was 20-0 entering the UFC 333 main event against Volkanovski, but he lost in the second round by stoppage, marking the first loss of his MMA career. It wasn’t surprising to see Evloev lose the fight, as Volkanovski is an amazing fighter, but to see Evloev get knocked out was pretty shocking given he had never tasted defeat before during his UFC career. Movsar Evloev Comments on UFC 333 Loss Taking to his social media, Evloev issued a statement following his loss at UFC 333 against Volkanovski. “Alhamdulillah for everything. Today wasn’t my day. Everything is written by Allah, and I accept whatever He has planned for me. Congratulations to Volk. He was the better man today. Thank you to the UFC for giving me the opportunity to fight for the title, and to all my fans,” Evloev wrote on his X . Alhamdulillah for everything. Today wasn’t my day. Everything is written by Allah, and I accept whatever He has planned for me. Congratulations to Volk. He was the better man today. Thank you to the UFC for giving me the opportunity to fight for the title, and to all my fans — Movsar Evloev (@MovsarUFC) October 25, 2026 What’s Next for Movsar Evloev? This was a difficult loss for Evloev, but it doesn’t mean that he won’t ever fight for the UFC featherweight title again. After all, he is 10-1 now in the UFC, and he had won 10 straight fights before that. So he has proven that he knows what it takes to get his hand raised inside the Octagon, and has done so ever since he entered the UFC several years ago. That being said, Evloev doesn’t typically finish fights, which is something the UFC matchmakers look for specifically when they are deciding who to push up the rankings. Evloev will likely have to fight down in the rankings now against someone who could be lower in the top 10. Taking a look at the UFC featherweight division, a matchup against Yair Rodriguez or Youssef Zalal may make the most sense, as Evloev has not fought either of those men yet, and he could make for an intriguing matchup for both. Regardless of who he faces next, Evloev likely needs to win like three straight fights before he can get back into the featherweight title picture, given there are other contenders still waiting around. On lap 74, Wood swept by and Mostert took over as his tail gunner, until the final lap when Wood surrendered and handed the place back. “That was an emotional last lap, I nearly looped it on the final lap,” said Feeney, who grew up a couple of miles from the track. “Even on Friday we were fast [in the dry], but I knew in the first stint it was not going to be easy. It’s Finals time, and we pulled another gear. We haven’t won since QR, and Bathurst was gut-wrenching. Mostert was a strong third, ahead of Wood and Brad Jones Racing ’s Andre Heimgartner , who ran a long opening stint so long that he made his first pitstop a lap before one lap before Brown made his second. Mostert was disappointed with his Qualifying performance. “Gutted that I didn’t qualify very well, it is so enjoyable to drive,” he admitted. “You do whatever you can for your team, I only just found out that Ryan did not make it in. I am gutted for him. But it all comes back to my mistake in Qualifying.” There were no Chevrolets among the top 14 finishers – but there was a reason why. In his first race as a full-time driver, Erebus Motorsport ’s Jarrod Hughes looked superb. He was bowling along in eighth place when suddenly he made a third pitstop for a splash of fuel. In doing so, he dropped back to 17th place. That stop was important for Anton De Pasquale . His Team 18 Chevrolet Camaro was all over the place in the first, wet Qualifying session and started the race from 21st. Then at the first corner, contact with another car flattened a tyre and by the end of the lap, after a fast pitstop, he was last. After Saturday’s result, ‘ADP’, who had qualified as a Finalist, was on the see-saw of making to the next round or not but when Wood passed Mostert, he fell onto the wrong side of the see-saw. That put Saturday’s result into perspective. Had Team 18 asked David Reynolds to slow, to advance De Pasquale, he would made qualified through to the next round. But when Hughes stopped for fuel – and a couple of laps later, another non-Finalist Chevrolet driven by PremiAir Racing ’s Cooper Murray – none of that mattered... So Wood, Kai Allen ( Grove Racing Ford) and Jack Le Brocq ( Matt Stone Racing Chevrolet) have been eliminated from the Finals, and seven drivers are still in contention. item.description: Brian Bishop-Imagn Images Virginia Tech HC James Franklin’s first move after beating Clemson? Helping the equipment staff appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Virginia Tech football made a late comeback at Memorial Stadium to secure its first win over the Clemson Tigers since 2007. James Franklin made a pivotal decision in the closing minutes, and the Hokies rewarded their head coach with a dramatic 20-16 win . However, following the memorable victory, the excited head coach attracted attention for his postgame actions. Old friends Dabo Swinney and Franklin faced each other as opposing head coaches for the first time in their careers on Saturday. Fortunately for Franklin, he walked away with the victory and took time to greet nearly everyone wearing Virginia Tech gear as they headed into the tunnel. The first-year Virginia Tech coach then doubled back and helped an equipment staff member push his cart. The victory improved the Hokies’ record to 6-2 after they managed just three wins last season. With the win, the former Penn State head coach also secured bowl eligibility in his first season at Virginia Tech. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Virginia Tech faced a crucial fourth-and-1 situation at Clemson’s five-yard line while trailing 16-13 late in the fourth quarter. Franklin could have sent kicker John Love onto the field to attempt a field goal and potentially force overtime. Instead, he trusted his offense to reach the end zone and take the lead. After the game, Franklin admitted that he had briefly considered settling for the field goal . However, his decision to go for the touchdown at such a critical moment paid off. During a sideline interview with ESPN, Franklin also highlighted his team’s composure and ability to avoid costly mistakes throughout the contest. “Well, we didn’t turn the ball over,” said Franklin to the ESPN broadcast. “For the most part, we didn’t have a bunch of penalties. Before you can learn to win games like this, you’ve got to figure out not to lose them. We lost two games because of that, but our guys have learned from that and grown from that and figured that out.’ The Hokies will now have a bye week before traveling to face SMU on November 6. item.title: Barcelona explored move for Real Madrid’s club-record signing but were put off by the price – Romano
item.description: Barcelona explored move for Real Madrid’s club-record signing but were put off by the price – Romano Barcelona explored the possibility of signing Yan Diomande at the beginning of the summer transfer window but ultimately considered the winger too expensive, according to a report relaying Fabrizio Romano’s information . The Ivorian eventually became Real Madrid’s club record signing, while the Catalans pursued a different attacking option in Karim Adeyemi. The contrasting transfer decisions offer an insight into how Barcelona and Real Madrid approached their summer recruitment. While Diomande’s price proved prohibitive for Barça , Adeyemi emerged as a more attainable opportunity after Borussia Dortmund offered the German winger to Madrid, who chose not to pursue the deal. Both players ultimately found their preferred destinations, with Adeyemi joining Barcelona to work under Hansi Flick . Real Madrid passed on Adeyemi before Barcelona moved Adeyemi’s transfer situation was influenced by his contract position at Borussia Dortmund. Barcelona inquired about the possibility of signing Yan Diomande. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images) With his deal due to expire in 2027, the winger was entering the final year of his contract and was unwilling to renew. He wanted to join Barcelona, giving the Catalans a significant advantage in negotiations. Jorge Mendes, Adeyemi’s agent, presented the opportunity to Barcelona as the club looked to reinforce its attacking options. Dortmund had to weigh the financial benefit of selling him against the risk of losing him for nothing when his contract expired. Real Madrid, meanwhile, decided against advancing with the opportunity because Adeyemi was not considered the right fit for the profile the club wanted. That decision left Barcelona better placed to negotiate for a player who had made his preference clear. Barcelona secured Adeyemi on favourable terms Barcelona ended up signing Adeyemi instead. (Photo by Francisco Macia/Getty Images) Barcelona initially offered €20 million for Adeyemi, but Dortmund rejected that proposal. The clubs eventually reached an agreement worth €22 million upfront plus €7 million in potential add-ons, with the transfer officially confirmed in July. Adeyemi signed a contract with Barcelona until 2031. The fee was made more attractive by the winger’s contract situation and his desire to leave. Adeyemi also brings versatility, having demonstrated that he can operate on either wing or through the middle. His pace gives Flick another option in attack as Barcelona look to build depth around their existing forward line. As for Diomande, Real Madrid ended up paying a whopping €125 million base fee, plus up to €15 million in potential add-ons.

Live Telecast: Sony Sports Network and SonyLIV (India), Sky Sport (New Zealand) Match result: TBD Player of the Match: TBD New Zealand A vs. India A: Score & Updates Welcome to CricketNews.com's live coverage of the unofficial Test between New Zealand A and India A at Lincoln. Day 2 updates New Zealand A held the upper hand on day two in Lincoln, having built a 204-run first-innings lead in the first four-day match against India A. India A lost openers KL Rahul and Yashasvi Jaiswal early in their second innings and were reduced to 10 for 2, which put them in trouble at once. Rahul was dismissed hit-wicket in the fifth over while trying to push away a ball that trickled toward the stumps off his inside edge. Devdutt Padikkal and B Sai Sudharsan then put together a third-wicket stand of 96 off 188 balls, which steadied the innings and kept the visitors in the contest. Stumps arrived with India A still 98 runs behind, Padikkal unbeaten on 56 and Sai Sudharsan on 39. Padikkal was given a reprieve during his 89-ball stay when Rhys Mariu dropped him at second slip off Kristian Clarke, whereas Sai Sudharsan’s 104-ball innings has been free of chances. Jaiswal (17 and 5) and Rahul (0 and 4), both expected to open in the Test series starting in the third week of November, got little time in the middle, facing only 77 balls between them in the match, 45 of them by Jaiswal in the first innings. Day 1 updates KL Rahul fell for an 8-ball duck, offering an edge in the third over. Yashasvi Jaiswal was also dismissed cheaply for 17 off 45 balls, caught behind off the moving new ball. Sai Sudharsan also departed for a 13-ball duck as India A were reduced to a precarious 44/3. Dhruv Jurel, Devdutt Padikkal, & Washington Sundar were also quick to depart, and India were 58/6 at one stage. Yash Rathod launched an aggressive counter-offensive against Fraser Sheat and Simon Keene. He finished as the top-scorer with a blistering 44 off 49 balls. Kiwi pacer Simon Keene bowled with immaculate seam presentation, tearing through the middle order with figures of 5/24 to break the spine of India A's batting. item.title: ‘Not welcome here’ – Nikola Jokic goes off on Nuggets fans who booed during OT win over Pelicans
item.description: Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post The Denver Nuggets were on the verge of being blown out by the New Orleans Pelicans, and their fans were less than impressed with the effort they showed. The Nuggets were down by 23 points at one point against the Pelicans, who are one of the weakest teams in the NBA. And while Jokic helped the team rally and earn a comeback win against the Pelicans in overtime, the franchise superstar wasn’t exactly happy with the way fans treated them during their comeback effort. Nikola Jokic says Denver Nuggets fans who booed them should not attend future games Speaking to reporters after the game, Nikola Jokic said he didn’t appreciate the fans who booed them at the Ball Arena and that they shouldn’t attend a future game. He noted that the Nuggets have shown in the past that they are capable of coming back from large deficits, and that fans should have supported them more vocally rather than jeering them. Jokic said: “I think the fans that booed us are not welcome here anymore, if you ask me… if you guys follow us, you know that we never quit and we came back from much worse for similar situations. If you ask me, they’re not welcome anymore.” This was far from the first time that the Denver Nuggets have pulled off such a comeback at home. In February of 2020, the Nuggets pulled off a near-identical 23-point comeback against the San Antonio Spurs, albeit doing so in regulation rather than overtime. The Nuggets are now 1-1 to start the season, getting their first win after their season-opening loss to the Oklahoma City Thunder. Coming into the season, there were many concerns that the Nuggets had not built a strong enough roster around Nikola Jokic to compete for the NBA championship in a stacked Western Conference. So far, even with their win against the Pelicans, the Nuggets have shown that those concerns were valid, and they have a lot to work on as the season goes on. item.title: Texas QB Arch Manning Drops Honest Quote After Win Over Ole Miss
item.description: AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 24: Arch Manning #16 of the Texas Longhorns warms up before the game against the Ole Miss Rebels at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium on October 24, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images) Getty The No. 19 Texas Longhorns entered Saturday night with a must-win mindset against the No. 7 Ole Miss Rebels. Nobody played with a bigger chip on his shoulder than Texas quarterback Arch Manning, who hasn’t had the season many envisioned so far. The criticism was loud in Austin this week. Despite some misfires throughout the game, Manning delivered several stellar moments and helped lead the Longhorns to a massive 34-27 win. Manning completed 18 of 30 passes for 212 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions while adding two rushing touchdowns. He also lost a fumble on a sack after an Ole Miss defender beat Texas’ left tackle off the line of scrimmage. Manning Drops Honest Quote After Win Following the victory, Manning opened up during his postgame press conference about the emotions he felt after last weekend’s loss. “It was a hard Sunday when I went over to their place, damn near bawled crying over to them,” Manning said of seeing his family. “So just being able to see them after a game after a win felt good.” #Texas QB Arch Manning says last Sunday was a tough day. He spent it with his parents, bawling crying. Plus, what does an “Edgy Arch” looks like in practice. @ontexasfootball https://t.co/riWKfXQSeo — CJ Vogel (@CJVogel_OTF) October 25, 2026 Manning also said he likes when people count him out after a lifetime of hype and high expectations. “I’ve been hyped up all my life… I think I kind of like being, you know, disregarded and counted out,” Manning added, via Inside Texas. Steve Sarkisian Praises Manning After Victory Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian was quick to praise Manning after the gritty win. “The guys see it. They see him get up. They see him fiery, you know,” Sarkisian said. “They see him high step in the end zone on the touchdown at the end. The guys like that stuff, you know. And that’s part of our DNA too; it’s cut from his cloth. And so I think it’s helpful.” Looking at Texas While this was a big win for Texas, and the Longhorns should certainly enjoy it, they still have some massive games on their schedule that they’ll need to win. They’ll remain home next weekend when they take on Mississippi State on Oct. 31. After that, they’ll have back-to-back road games against No. 22 Missouri and No. 18 LSU before ending the regular season with a home matchup against Arkansas and a road rivalry game against Texas A&M. item.title: Julian Ward has done it, Liverpool's new midfield maestro is here
item.description: Julian Ward has done it, Liverpool's new midfield maestro is here Liverpool are crying out for a new midfield maestro and he is here. Andoni Iraola's squad is in a real crisis when it comes to the midfield department. With Dominik Szoboszlai sidelined and Ryan Gravenberch having to play right-back, Iraola's first reserve is James McConnell. With all respect to McConnell, who will go onto have a successful career, he isn't quite at the level Liverpool need him to be right now. This is a midfielder who struggled to get regular game time at Ajax. Trey Nyoni is a fantastic option. He's definitely ready to be starting games for the Reds. Alexis Mac Allister has always been world-class, too, and he's showing that this season. But Liverpool need more depth. Whether that's as entering the market, or by promoting academy talent from within. Liverpool's plans to buy a midfielder in January Julian Ward's responsibility will be to address this midfield crisis in the January window. He has a lot of pressure on his hands to fix some of the mistakes his predecessor, Richard Hughes, made. In terms of who the Reds could be targeting. Some of the players mentioned who are on Liverpool's radar includes Lamine Camara. The Reds have been scouting him for a long-time. They are well aware of the Senegalese international's quality. Liverpool first wanted to sign him back in 2024, as an alternative to Martin Zubimendi but Arne Slot vetoed the move. This summer a move came close for Camara and it's expected Liverpool will return in the winter market. Other players to keep an eye on includes Alex Scott as well, who is well liked by Iraola. Liverpool's new midfield maestro is Luca Eden But while signing Camara or someone of his ilk is essential in the winter market, Liverpool also have a new midfield maestro. Luca Eden has arrived on the scene. The 15-year-old has been a sensation this season for Liverpool making seven goal contributions in nine games. His latest goal against Manchester United was an incredible hit from long-range. The type of goal you have seen Steven Gerrard score time and time again. With moments like that, the comparisons won't go away. Liverpool know they have an extremely talented player in Eden. He's a real midfield maestro, who can pull the strings in midfield and win games on his own. Eden is technically brilliant, he is hard and aggressive with his tackles and he has a great shot on him. When you watch him play, you sit back and say: Liverpool have done it

item.title: 'This is the only Clasico' - Mourinho's Real trying to stop Barca's shot at history
item.description: [Getty Images] Barcelona stand on the brink of La Liga history, targeting a 10th consecutive victory to start the league season. It will surpass the mark set in 1968-69 by Real Madrid, who will have the chance to end that remarkable run on Sunday when the sides meet at Camp Nou. Barcelona head into El Clasico on the back of a 4-2 Champions League defeat by Paris St-Germain , giving Jose Mourinho's men the perfect opportunity to capitalise on that setback and wreck the record bid of their rivals. 'Madrid with Mourinho wins trophies' Real boss Mourinho has insisted his team's most recent performances, two 4-1 victories against Sevilla and RB Leipzig , would count for little in a fixture that has such global appeal and standing. "We are in a good dynamic, we play well, we score goals, but the Clasico is different. What we have done before has no influence," he said. "There are other important matches in the world, but this is the only Clasico, the world stops." Some of football's biggest names with be involved, with six of this year's 30 Ballon d'Or nominees available - Barcelona's Pau Cubarsi, Rodri and Lamine Yamal, and Real Madrid trio Marc Cucurella, Jude Bellingham and Kylian Mbappe. There will be huge individual battles between them on the pitch too. Cucurella could find himself trying to stop national team-mate Lamine Yamal down Barcelona's right, while centre-back Cubarsi could once again face Mbappe, renewing their rivalry after Spain's 2-0 victory over France in the World Cup semi-final. Striker Mbappe, though, has been in prolific form for Real, scoring 12 goals in 12 appearances this season. In midfield, Rodri and Bellingham could provide another fascinating clash between two of the game's leading players. With a six-point gap to leaders Barcelona, Mourinho acknowledged his third-placed side were still adapting to his methods and argued comparisons with more established teams were premature. "We've been together for three months if you take away pre-season and international breaks," he said. "The players are still getting to know me and the way I do things." He also dismissed the idea of making sweeping tactical changes specifically to contain Lamine Yamal. "He's a great player, we respect great players. We aren't going to completely change things. A compact defensive shape, disciplined pressing and quick transitions could force Barcelona away from their preferred rhythm. Rather than chasing possession, Madrid must remain organised and choose the right moments to attack. Lamine Yamal will be central to Barcelona's attacking plans, while Madrid will look to use their pace and quality in the final third to test the home defence. The midfield battle will also be crucial. If Madrid can win second balls and prevent Barcelona from finding space between the lines, they can reduce the pressure on their defence. Set-pieces could provide another route to goal and Flick specifically identified them as a threat. "We know Real Madrid's strengths, and they're among the best at set-pieces," he said. "We have to defend better than we did in Paris." For Barcelona, victory would not only set a record, but strengthen their position as clear early-season title favourites, opening up a nine-point lead over Real Madrid. For Mourinho's men, halting that run would reduce the deficit to three points and deliver a major psychological boost to revive their hopes of domestic success this season. item.title: Dana White Reacts to Alexander Volkov’s UFC 333 Performance
item.description: Dana White Alexander Volkov UFC 333 Getty UFC president Dana White shared his reaction to heavyweight contender Alexander Volkov’s performance at UFC 333. In a main-card heavyweight bout, Volkov defeated Rizvan Kuniev via unanimous decision to extend his current win streak to three straight fights. Volkov has now won seven of his last eight fights as he continues to climb the UFC heavyweight rankings and get closer to an elusive title shot. Dana White Comments on Alexander Volkov’s UFC 333 Outing Speaking to the media after UFC 333, White commented on Volkov’s outing against Kuniev, while responding to a reporter’s question about whether or not the performance was good enough to get a title shot. “He had a good performance tonight, and we’ll see what happens next,” White said. The UFC president was also asked about a viral clip that happened at the UFC 333 pre-fight press conference, where White did not appear to recognize Volkov, who was in the audience asking a question. White, however, is adamant he knew it was Volkov all along. “Yeah, of course I knew it was him. And if I didn’t know it was him, (Alexander) Volkanovski said it to me three times. He said, ‘You know who that is, right?’ I said, ‘Yeah, I know who that is.’ That isn’t the first time that a fighter has gone up there and done an interview or asked a question. I thought it was like a schtick he was doing, and I was waiting for the punchline, and it never came. We only did the co-main and main, and I’m assuming that he thought he would be able to be a part of the press conference and say, ‘Hey man, I want my title shot,’ and that’s what that was, not like some schtick he was trying to do,” White said. Alexander Volkov Closing in on Title Shot Now riding a three-fight win streak, Volkov is likely one more win away at worst from getting a title shot against the winner of the UFC 334 heavyweight title fight between champion Ciryl Gane and Josh Hokit , and he very well be next in line to fight the winner. However, Volkov will have to wait and see what happens between Sergei Pavlovich and Alex Pereira at UFC 335, as the winner of that bout could get the next title shot instead. We’ll see what happens, but Volkov surely put himself in a good position with the big win over Kuniev. item.title: Ballon d’Or ceremony returns to England in nod to ‘revolutionary’ Stanley Matthews
item.description: Matthews’ family ‘very excited’ as London Palladium hosts event 70 years after first award at Blackpool town hall When football’s dignitaries assemble on Monday at the London Palladium for the Ballon d’Or ceremony it will be a far cry from the first awards 70 years ago. That was held in the slightly less glamorous surroundings of Blackpool town hall, where Stanley Matthews was presented with the prize by Gabriel Hanot, the visionary editor of L’Équipe who came up with the idea of crowning the world’s best player every year. A specially commissioned china plate was also handed over by the town’s mayor before the 41-year-old Matthews, who was famously teetotal, gave a short speech. “He might have had a double carrot juice that day,” says his son, Stanley Matthews Jr, who will attend this year’s awards with his sister, Jean, and her two daughters. “There was no ceremony. ‘Here’s your Ballon d’Or, well done’, sort of thing. But obviously it’s grown over the years, and now it’s a huge event. We’re very excited.” Continue reading...

The foul not only checked a promising break, but broke a bone in Coluna’s foot. item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. item.title: Is el clásico still the world’s biggest match? Three questions before Barcelona v Real Madrid
item.description: The fixture’s relevance waned as the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded. Can Lamine Yamal and Mbappé lift it into a new era? For the best part of a decade, el clásico was more than just soccer’s biggest fixture. It was the defining narrative. At the peak of the Lionel Messi v Cristiano Ronaldo era, there were clásicos everywhere. Yes, when the two historic rivals clashed on the pitch, but also in the voting for the Ballon d’Or every year and in so much of the discourse around the sport. As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. In 2026, however, it’s difficult to measure a clásico ’s standing. Is it still the sport’s biggest fixture? Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
